text: The number of integral values of m so that the abscissa of point of intersection of lines 3x + 4y = 9 and y = mx + 1 is also an integer, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
3x + 4(mx + 1) = 9

$\Rightarrow$ x(3 + 4m) = 5

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\frac{5}{(3+4m)}$

$\Rightarrow$ (3 + 4m) = $\pm$1, $\pm$5

$\Rightarrow$ 4m = $-$3 $\pm$ 1, $-$3 $\pm$ 5 

$\Rightarrow$ 4m = $-$4, $-$2, $-$8, 2

$\Rightarrow$ m = $-$1, $-\frac{1}{2}$, $-$2, $\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ Two integral value of m.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

If the system of equations (in u, v, w) given by $α$u + $β$v + $γ$w = 0, $β$u + $γ$v + $α$w = 0; $γ$u + $α$v + $β$w = 0 has non-trivial solution, then the value of $\frac{a^{2}}{b}$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{3} + ax^{2} + bx + c = 0$ 

Roots are $α$, $β$, $γ$.

For non-trivial solutions,

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} α & β & γ \\ β & γ & α \\ γ & α & β \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $α^{3}+β^{3}+γ^{3}-3αβγ=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(α+β+γ)\left [(α+β+γ)^{2}-3(\sum αβ)\right ]=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(-a)[a^{2}-3b]=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $a^{2}=3b$ ($\because$ a $\neq$ 0)

$\Rightarrow \frac{a^{2}}{b}=3$

text: The equation of one of the straight lines which passes through the point (1, 3) and makes an angles $\tan ^{-1}\left (\sqrt{2}\right )$ with the straight line, y + 1 = 3$\sqrt{2}$ x is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
Let slope of line be m

$\therefore$ $\left |\frac{m-3\sqrt{2}}{1+3\sqrt{2}m}\right |=\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow m-3\sqrt{2}=\pm \sqrt{2}\pm 6m$

$\Rightarrow m\mp 6m=\pm \sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow m=-\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{5}$ or $\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{7}$

Hence line can be

$y-3=\frac{-4\sqrt{2}}{5}(x-1)$

$\Rightarrow 5y-15=-4\sqrt{2}x+4\sqrt{2}$

$\Rightarrow 4\sqrt{2}x+5y-(15+4\sqrt{2})=0$

text:
If the functions are defined as $f(x)=\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=\sqrt{1-x}$, then what is the common domain of the following functions :

f + g, f $-$ g, f/g, g/f, g $-$ f where $(f\pm g)(x)=f(x)\pm g(x),(f/g)x=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f+g=\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{1-x}$

$\Rightarrow x\geq 0$ & $1-x\geq 0\Rightarrow x\in [0,1]$

$f-g=\sqrt{x}-\sqrt{1-x}$

$\Rightarrow x\geq 0$ & $1-x\geq 0\Rightarrow x\in [0,1]$

$f/g=\frac{\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{1-x}}$

$\Rightarrow x\geq 0$ & $1-x>0\Rightarrow x\in [0,1)$

$g/f=\frac{\sqrt{1-x}}{\sqrt{x}}$

$\Rightarrow 1-x\geq 0$ & $x>0\Rightarrow x\in (0,1]$

$g-f=\sqrt{1-x}-\sqrt{x}$

$\Rightarrow 1-x\geq 0$ & $x\geq 0\Rightarrow x\in [0,1]$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\in (0,1)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: If $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{|x|} & ;\; |x|\geq 1 \\ ax^{2}+b & ;\; |x|<1 \end{array} \right.$ is differentiable at every point of the domain, then the values of a and b are respectively :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{1}{|x|}, & |x|\geq 1 \\ ax^{2}+b, & |x|<1 \end{array} \right.$

$=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} -\frac{1}{x}; & x\leq -1 \\ ax^{2}+b; & -1<x<1 \\ \frac{1}{x}; & x\geq 1 \end{array} \right.$

As f(x) is differentiable so it is also continuous,

 at x = 1,

$\lim _{x\to 1^{-}}f(x)=\lim _{x\to 1^{+}}f(x)$

$\Rightarrow a+b=\frac{1}{1}$

$\Rightarrow a+b=1$ ...... (1)

As f(x) is differentiable, so at x = 1

L.H.D. = R.H.D.

$\Rightarrow 2ax=-\frac{1}{x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow 2a=-1$

$\Rightarrow a=-\frac{1}{2}$

From (1), $b=\frac{3}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: Let $A+2B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 3 \\ -5 & 3 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ and $2A-B=\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]$. If Tr(A) denotes the sum of all diagonal elements of the matrix A, then Tr(A) $-$ Tr(B) has value equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$A=\frac{1}{5}((A+2B)+2(2A-B))$

$=\frac{1}{5}⎛⎝⎜\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 6 & -3 & 3 \\ -5 & 3 & 1 \end{array}\right ]+\left [\begin{array}{lll} 4 & -2 & 10 \\ 4 & -2 & 12 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \end{array}\right ]⎞⎠⎟$

$=\frac{1}{5}\left [\begin{array}{lll} 5 & 0 & 10 \\ 10 & -5 & 15 \\ -5 & 5 & 5 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow tr(A)=1$

Similarly,

$B=\frac{1}{5}(2(A+2B)-(2A-B))$

$=\frac{1}{5}⎛⎝⎜\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 4 & 0 \\ 12 & -6 & 6 \\ -10 & 6 & 2 \end{array}\right ]-\left [\begin{array}{lll} 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array}\right ]⎞⎠⎟$

$=\frac{1}{5}\left [\begin{array}{lll} 0 & 6 & -5 \\ 10 & -5 & 0 \\ -10 & 5 & 0 \end{array}\right ]\Rightarrow tr(B)=-1$

$Tr(A)-Tr(B)=1-(-1)=2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: The sum of all the 4-digit distinct numbers that can be formed with the digits 1, 2, 2 and 3 is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The digits $1,2,2,3$ give $\dfrac{4!}{2!}=12$ distinct numbers.

Fix a digit in any one place. With 1 there, the digits $2,2,3$ fill the other places in $\dfrac{3!}{2!}=3$ ways; with 2 there, the digits $1,2,3$ fill them in $3!=6$ ways; with 3 there, the digits $1,2,2$ fill them in $3$ ways.

So over all 12 numbers, the digits in each place add up to $1\times 3+2\times 6+3\times 3=24$.

$\text{Sum}=24\times (1000+100+10+1)=24\times 1111=26664$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: The value of $3+\frac{1}{4+\frac{1}{3+\dfrac{1}{4+\dfrac{1}{3+....\infty }}}}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $x=3+\frac{1}{4+\frac{1}{3+\dfrac{1}{4+\dfrac{1}{3+....\infty }}}}$

So, $x=3+\frac{1}{4+\frac{1}{x}}=3+\frac{1}{\frac{4x+1}{x}}$

$\Rightarrow (x-3)=\frac{x}{(4x+1)}$

$\Rightarrow (4x+1)(x-3)=x$

$\Rightarrow 4x^{2}-12x+x-3=x$

$\Rightarrow 4x^{2}-12x-3=0$

$x=\frac{12\pm \sqrt{(12)^{2}+12\times 4}}{2\times 4}=\frac{12\pm \sqrt{12(16)}}{8}$

$=\frac{12\pm 4\times 2\sqrt{3}}{8}=\frac{3\pm 2\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$x=\frac{3}{2}\pm \sqrt{3}=1.5\pm \sqrt{3}$.

But only positive value is accepted

So, x = $1.5+\sqrt{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: Let $z_{1}, z_{2}$ be the roots of the equation $z^{2} + az + 12 = 0$ and $z_{1}, z_{2}$ form an equilateral triangle with origin. Then, the value of |a| is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The points $z_{1}$, $z_{2}$ and $z_{3}=0$ form an equilateral triangle, so

$z_{1}^{2}+z_{2}^{2}+z_{3}^{2}=z_{1}z_{2}+z_{2}z_{3}+z_{3}z_{1}\Rightarrow z_{1}^{2}+z_{2}^{2}=z_{1}z_{2}$

From $z^{2}+az+12=0$: $z_{1}+z_{2}=-a$ and $z_{1}z_{2}=12$.

Adding $2z_{1}z_{2}$ to both sides:

$(z_{1}+z_{2})^{2}=3z_{1}z_{2}\Rightarrow a^{2}=3\times 12=36$

So $a=\pm 6$ and $|a|=6$.

Hence, the answer is 6.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: The mean age of 25 teachers in a school is 40 years. A teacher retires at the age of 60 years and a new teacher is appointed in his place. If the mean age of the teachers in this school now is 39 years, then the age (in years) of the newly appointed teacher is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mean $(x–)$ = $\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}.....+x_{n}}{n}$ = $\frac{\sum x}{n}$

Here, Mean = 40 of 25 teachers

$\therefore$ 40 = $\frac{\sum x}{25}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sum x$ = 40 $\times$ 25 = 1000

After retireing of a 60 year old teacher, total age of 24 teachers, 

$x_{1} + x_{2} + . . . . . .x_{24} = 1000$ $-$ 60 = 940

Now a new teacher of age A year is appointed. 

$\therefore$ Now total age of this 25 teachers 

$x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3} + . . . . . + x_{25} = 940 + A$

$\therefore$ Mean age = $\frac{940+A}{25}$

According to question,

$\frac{940+A}{25}$ = 39

$\Rightarrow$ A = 35
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: If $f(x)=\int \frac{5x^{8}+7x^{6}}{(x^{2}+1+2x^{7})^{2}}dx,(x\geq 0),f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=\frac{1}{K}$, then the value of K is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\int \frac{5x^{8}+7x^{6}}{(2x^{7}+x^{2}+1)^{2}}dx=\int \frac{5x^{8}+7x^{6}}{x^{14}\left (2+\frac{1}{x5}+\frac{1}{x7}\right )^{2}}dx$

$\int \frac{\frac{5}{x6}+\frac{7}{x8}}{\left (2+\frac{1}{x5}+\frac{1}{x7}\right )^{2}}dx$

put $2+\frac{1}{x^{5}}+\frac{1}{x^{7}}=t$

$\Rightarrow -\left (\frac{5}{x^{6}}+\frac{7}{x^{8}}\right )dx=dt$

$\int \frac{-dt}{t^{2}}=\frac{1}{t}+c$

$\Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1}{2+\frac{1}{x5}+\frac{1}{x7}}+C=\frac{x^{7}}{2x^{7}+1+x^{2}}+C$

$f(0)=0\Rightarrow C=0$

$f(x)=\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{k}$

$\Rightarrow k=4$

text: A square ABCD has all its vertices on the curve $x^{2}y^{2} = 1$. The midpoints of its sides also lie on the same curve. Then, the square of area of ABCD is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The curve $x^{2}y^{2}=1$ is the pair $xy=\pm 1$: four branches, one in each quadrant, symmetric about $O$. The square has its centre at $O$ and one vertex on each branch.


[IMG]

Let $B\left (p,\dfrac{1}{p}\right )$ lie on $xy=1$. The half-diagonals $OA$ and $OB$ are equal and perpendicular, so $A$ is $B$ turned through $90^{\circ }$ clockwise about $O$:

$A\left (\dfrac{1}{p},-p\right )=\left (q,-\dfrac{1}{q}\right ),q=\dfrac{1}{p}$

The midpoint of $AB$, $P\left (\dfrac{p+\frac{1}{p}}{2},\dfrac{\frac{1}{p}-p}{2}\right )$, lies on the curve:

$\left (p+\dfrac{1}{p}\right )^{2}\left (\dfrac{1}{p}-p\right )^{2}=16\Rightarrow \left (p^{2}-\dfrac{1}{p^{2}}\right )^{2}=16$

Then

$OB^{4}=\left (p^{2}+\dfrac{1}{p^{2}}\right )^{2}=\left (p^{2}-\dfrac{1}{p^{2}}\right )^{2}+4=20\Rightarrow OB^{2}=2\sqrt{5}$

Each diagonal is $2~OB$, so the area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(2OB)^{2}=2OB^{2}=4\sqrt{5}$, and its square is $(4\sqrt{5})^{2}=80$.

Hence, the answer is 80.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift
